messages:
sara-m: Heads-up — StreamlineAI (customer) opened a high-severity ticket: repeated 5xx / timeouts from hosted inference since ~2026-03-17T08:12Z. They see a cluster of 504s and request timeouts. p95 ~6s, p99 >12s. They included a few request IDs.

support-bot: Ticket #3571 created, assigned to infra oncall @tyler-r.

tyler-r: looking at hosted-ingress-prod metrics now. I can reproduce a spike in request_queue_depth for the tenant route (route=streamline-latency) — hitting configured max_depth (512) and we see continuous-batching backlog growth.

sara-m: customer says errors started after a burst of requests from a batch job. They attached sample request-id: r-0a1b2c3d.

tyler-r: logs show a ton of pending slots: 
```
INGRESS_POOL queue_depth=512 max_depth=512 requests_waiting=210 batching_backlog=128 kv_cache_misses=42
gateway_error: upstream_timeout -> rejection
```

tyler-r: Also seeing `dequeue_time` tail spikes and worker batchers not catching up. Continuous batching window is accumulating.

alex-g: can you paste the exact metric query you ran? I want to correlate with model-side latency.

tyler-r: query used: `sum(rate(requests_total{route=~"streamline.*",env="prod"}[1m])) by (route)` and `max_over_time(request_queue_depth[5m])` — attaching a short flamegraph.

kevin-s: mitigation options: short-term -> disable continuous batching for that tenant route, or raise `max_depth` and `max_concurrent_dequeue` and enable burst_capacity for Dedicated-like behavior. Medium -> tune batching window to avoid long prefix accumulation for short requests.

sara-m: customer needs a fast workaround. Can we flip a per-route flag?

tyler-r: yes — can push a per-route config change: `continuous_batching.enabled=false` for route=streamline-latency. I'll run a canary on one host.

ops-bot: runbook step: `ingressctl set-route --route streamline-latency --continuous-batching false --rollback 10m`

tyler-r: running the change now on canary (host: ing-canary-7). Will watch queue_depth and latency.

(5m later)

tyler-r: Canary applied: queue_depth dropped from 512->120 over 90s, p99 backend latency for that route down from ~12s -> ~2.3s. Customer reports reduced 504s.

sara-m: customer confirmed error rate declined. They're still worried about a long-term fix.

alex-g: follow-ups: 1) figure out why continuous batching window grew — workload had many short requests causing batching to wait for prefixes, 2) add a per-tenant safety throttle that auto-disables batching when backlog > 80% for 30s, 3) consider kv_cache prewarm for common prefixes.

kevin-s: also recommend adding an alert: `request_queue_depth > 400 for 1m` -> page oncall and auto-trigger per-route mitigation job.

tyler-r: created a short postmortem stub and an action item list. I'll schedule a deeper root cause analysis with ML infra to investigate model-side dequeue slowdowns and kernel stalls.

support-bot: Updated ticket #3571: mitigation applied, customer notified, follow-ups scheduled.

sara-m: thanks — keeping this thread for the postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
